---
title: "Quickstart"
---

## Run the digital twin in 60 seconds

1. Activate your venv (`source .venv/bin/activate`).
2. Run `python -m braccio_twin` to bring up the headless PyBullet session.
3. In a second terminal, start the FastAPI bridge: `uvicorn web.backend.app:app --reload --port 8011`.
4. In a third terminal, run the frontend dev server: `cd web/frontend && VITE_BACKEND_ORIGIN=http://localhost:8011 npm run dev`.
5. Open `http://localhost:5173` in your browser. The viewer renders the Braccio and telemetry streams over the WebSocket.

## Run the curses controller against real hardware

1. Connect the Arduino Mega at `/dev/ttyACM0` and the Teensy 4.1 at `/dev/ttyACM1`.
2. Run `python -m braccio_ctrl /dev/ttyACM0 --teensy-port /dev/ttyACM1`.
3. Press `H` to home the arm, `Z` to toggle the autonomous sweep, or `M` to open the saved-states menu.
4. Press `ESC` to quit.

The `safety/` stack is always on; every manual keypress routes through `SafetyAPI.plan_and_validate` before the servos move.

## Edit a sequence in the curses editor

1. Save a named pose. With the arm in position, press `M` to open the states menu, press `n` to add a new state, type a name, and confirm.
2. Press `F4` (or whatever the current binding is in the controller help bar) to open the sequence editor.
3. Write DSL text. See the [command reference](../dsl/commands.qmd) for syntax.
4. Press `F5` to run. Errors appear in red; the status bar shows `● RUNNING step N/M pass P/Q` while execution is in progress.
5. Press `F6` to stop.

## Build the SPA for GitHub Pages

The frontend ships a demo mode that replaces the Run button with a Copy-DSL button and routes every backend call through a localStorage-backed mock. Build with:

```bash
cd web/frontend
VITE_BASE=/Reactive-Robot/editor/ VITE_DEMO_MODE=true npm run build
```

The `dist/` directory is the artifact the Pages workflow uploads.
